title: Private planning bootstrap
description:
Private planning/bootstrap epic for auxide-io (CPAL I/O layer). Tracks device selection, error recovery, sample-rate negotiation, input/duplex recording, latency reporting, channel routing, RT-clean callbacks, and README reconciliation. Children own their DoD. Closes only after all children are individually completable with populated acceptance + design.

## Success Criteria
- Every child bead (auxide-io-*) has non-empty acceptance and design.
- `cargo test -p auxide-io` and `cargo clippy -p auxide-io -- -D warnings` green across the crate.
design: PLAN: Tracker only. After children close, re-run the io test/clippy gate and close this epic last.
acceptance_criteria:
GATED EXIT — epic closes only when:
1. Every child bead (auxide-io-*) has non-empty `--acceptance` and `--design`.
2. `cargo test -p auxide-io` and `cargo clippy -p auxide-io -- -D warnings` green across the crate.

title: Repair auxide-io runtime API drift
description: Fix the current integration break between auxide and auxide-io around RuntimeHandle and sample-rate/block-size access so the suite compiles cleanly again.
notes: Closed after the auxide runtime API drift was resolved and validated with cargo test -p auxide-io and cargo test --workspace.

title: Reconcile README with the real StreamController API
description:
Reconcile README.md with the real StreamController API. The README was written against an earlier API and now disagrees with stream_controller.rs (play_handle, RuntimeHandle, ChannelMap, error recovery). A reader copying README examples should get code that compiles.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `cargo test -p auxide-io` green; clippy clean.
2. Every Rust snippet in README.md compiles against the current public API (verified by extracting snippets into a doc-test or `examples/` built in CI, or manual review).
3. README documents both `play` (legacy) and `play_handle` (new) and the RuntimeHandle + RuntimeControl control flow accurately.
4. API names in README (get_best_sample_rate, start/stop, error_flag) match the code.

## Design
A. Read stream_controller.rs public signatures; rewrite README examples to match.
B. Move key example into `examples/stream_example.rs` and ensure it builds, referencing it from README; or mark snippets `rust,no_run` doctests.
C. Fix stale names. Iterate until README examples build.
design:
PLAN:
A. Read stream_controller.rs public signatures and rewrite README examples to match (play_handle takes RuntimeHandle; control via RuntimeControl).
B. Move the key example into `examples/stream_example.rs` and ensure it builds (`cargo build --example stream_example`), referencing it from README; or mark snippets as `rust,no_run` doctests.
C. Fix any stale method/type names. Iterate until README examples build.
acceptance_criteria:
GATED EXIT — all must hold:
1. `cargo test -p auxide-io` green; `cargo clippy -p auxide-io -- -D warnings` clean.
2. Every Rust snippet in README.md compiles against the current public API (verified by extracting snippets into a doc-test or `examples/` that is built in CI, OR a manual review pass).
3. README documents both `play` (legacy) and `play_handle` (new architecture) and the `RuntimeHandle` + `RuntimeControl` control flow accurately, matching stream_controller.rs signatures.
4. API names in README (get_best_sample_rate, start/stop, error_flag) match the code.

title: Remove eprintln from the audio callback (RT violation)
description:
Remove eprintln/println from the audio callback (RT violation). stream_controller.rs uses eprintln for overflow errors and periodic diagnostics every 50 callbacks. Printing allocates and can block in the RT thread. Replace with lock-free atomic diagnostics counters the main thread can drain.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `cargo test -p auxide-io` green; clippy clean.
2. grep for `eprintln!|println!` inside the audio callback closure (and shared callback helper) returns nothing.
3. A lock-free `Diagnostics` (atomics: callback_count, overflow_count, peak) is updated instead; NEW `StreamController::diagnostics() -> DiagnosticsSnapshot` lets the main thread read them without allocating in the callback.
4. NEW `callback_no_alloc` test: run shared callback with a counting allocator, assert 0 allocations.

## Design
A. Add `Diagnostics { callback_count, overflow_count, peak }` (Arc) with the callback.
B. In shared callback (9k4), replace eprintln blocks with atomic increments; remove "every 50" eprintln.
C. Add `pub fn diagnostics(&self) -> DiagnosticsSnapshot`.
D. Add `#[cfg(test)] callback_no_alloc`. Iterate.
design:
PLAN:
A. Add `Diagnostics { callback_count: AtomicUsize, overflow_count: AtomicUsize, peak: AtomicU32 (f32 bits) }` shared (Arc) with the callback.
B. In the shared callback (auxide-io-9k4), replace the eprintln blocks with atomic increments / peak store; remove the "every 50" eprintln.
C. Add `pub fn diagnostics(&self) -> DiagnosticsSnapshot` reading the atomics.
D. Add `#[cfg(test)] callback_no_alloc`. Iterate until green.
acceptance_criteria:
GATED EXIT — all must hold:
1. `cargo test -p auxide-io` green; `cargo clippy -p auxide-io -- -D warnings` clean.
2. grep for `eprintln!|println!` inside the audio callback closure (and shared callback helper) returns nothing.
3. A lock-free `Diagnostics` (atomics: callback_count, overflow_count, max_sample_peak) is updated instead; NEW `StreamController::diagnostics() -> DiagnosticsSnapshot` lets the main thread read them without allocating in the callback.
4. NEW test `callback_no_alloc` (mirrors auxide-dsp-85b): run the shared callback with a counting allocator and assert 0 allocations during the callback.

title: Unify play and play_handle duplicated callbacks
description:
Unify the duplicated audio-callback bodies in `play` (stream_controller.rs:125) and `play_handle` (stream_controller.rs:239). They are near-identical copy-paste. Extract one shared callback closure/fn to remove drift and the RT-violating eprintln (see auxide-io-2d0).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `cargo test -p auxide-io` green; clippy clean.
2. A single shared callback helper (e.g., `run_callback`) used by both play and play_handle; no duplicated body remains (grep: callback logic appears once).
3. The shared helper contains no eprintln/println (RT-safe).

## Design
A. Define private generic `run_callback(data, info, state, error_flag, fill: impl Fn(&mut [f32]) -> Result<()>)`.
B. Rewrite play/play_handle to call run_callback with their fill closures.
C. Move periodic diagnostics to atomic counters (auxide-io-2d0). Add contract test. Iterate.
design:
PLAN:
A. Define a private generic `run_callback` taking the fill closure (one for Runtime, one for RuntimeHandle) plus shared state/error_flag/diagnostics atomics.
B. Rewrite `play`/`play_handle` to call `run_callback` with their respective fill closures.
C. Move periodic diagnostics to atomic counters (see auxide-io-2d0), removing eprintln.
D. Add `#[cfg(test)]` contract test still passes. Iterate until green.
acceptance_criteria:
GATED EXIT — all must hold:
1. `cargo test -p auxide-io` green; `cargo clippy -p auxide-io -- -D warnings` clean.
2. A single shared callback helper (e.g., `fn run_callback<T>(data, info, state, error_flag, fill: impl Fn(&mut [f32]) -> Result<()>)`) is used by both `play` and `play_handle`; no duplicated body remains (grep: callback logic appears once).

title: Add input and duplex recording support
description:
Add input and duplex (input+output) recording support. Today StreamController only builds output streams. To capture mic/line-in or build a full duplex synth, we need input and duplex stream construction plus a recorder that persists input to a WAV file (hound) or an in-memory ring buffer.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `cargo test -p auxide-io` green; clippy clean.
2. NEW `Recorder` (src/recorder.rs) with `push_block(&[f32])` and `save_wav(path)` (hound). Unit-test round-trips (write tiny WAV, read back, samples match).
3. `StreamController::play_input(...)` and `play_duplex(...)` build cpal input/duplex streams feeding input frames into the Recorder (logic tested directly, no device).
4. Document duplex wiring: input port count matches device input channels.

## Design
A. Add `hound` to dev-deps.
B. `Recorder { buf, sr, channels }` with push_block + save_wav.
C. `play_input` via build_input_stream; `play_duplex` via build_duplex_stream (input→Recorder, runtime→output).
D. Add round-trip test. Iterate.
design:
PLAN:
A. Add `hound` to dev-deps (and deps if used at runtime) for WAV writing.
B. Add `Recorder { buf: Vec<f32>, sr, channels }` with `push_block` and `save_wav`.
C. Add `play_input(device, sample_rate, recorder)` using `device.build_input_stream(...)`; `play_duplex` using `build_duplex_stream` feeding input→Recorder and running runtime→output.
D. Add the `#[cfg(test)]` round-trip test. Iterate until green.
acceptance_criteria:
GATED EXIT — all must hold:
1. `cargo test -p auxide-io` green; `cargo clippy -p auxide-io -- -D warnings` clean.
2. NEW `Recorder` type (src/recorder.rs or in stream_controller) with `push_block(&[f32])` that appends to an internal buffer and `save_wav(path)` (hound). Unit-test `push_block`+`save_wav` round-trips (write a tiny WAV, read it back, samples match).
3. `StreamController::play_input(...)` and `play_duplex(...)` constructors that build cpal input / duplex streams, feeding input frames into the Recorder (no device in tests; logic tested directly).
4. Document duplex wiring: input port count matches device input channels.

title: Remove or wire dead code (sample-rate helper, channel_router, handle no-ops, Paused state)
description:
Remove or wire dead code: `get_best_sample_rate` is implemented but unused by play/play_handle (see auxide-io-rfi), `channel_router` is unused (see auxide-io-uk1), and `handle_partial_block`/`handle_unknown_buffer_size` in buffer_size_adapter.rs are no-op stubs. Either wire them in or delete them so the crate has no orphaned API.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `cargo test -p auxide-io` green; clippy clean.
2. `get_best_sample_rate` is now called by play/play_handle (grep shows a call site).
3. `channel_router` is referenced by the adapter/StreamController (grep shows a call) OR removed.
4. `handle_partial_block`/`handle_unknown_buffer_size` are implemented (called) or deleted.
5. The `Paused` state is made meaningful OR documented as aliased to Stopped and removed.

## Design
A. Wire get_best_sample_rate via rfi; wire channel_router via uk1.
B. Implement handle_partial_block (progressive accumulation) and call it, or delete both stubs.
C. For Paused: remove the variant (keep Paused==Stopped semantics) updating stream_state.rs + callback; OR make Paused flush-and-hold. Choose remove for clarity.
D. After wiring/removing, run grep checks + cargo. Iterate.
design:
PLAN:
A. Wire get_best_sample_rate via auxide-io-rfi; wire channel_router via auxide-io-uk1.
B. Implement `handle_partial_block` (progressive accumulation for very small host buffers) and call it, or delete both stubs.
C. For Paused: define behavior (emit silence but keep stream alive vs Stopped which also silences) — simplest is to keep Paused == Stopped semantics and remove the variant, updating stream_state.rs + callback; OR make Paused flush-and-hold. Choose remove for clarity.
D. After wiring/removing, run grep checks + cargo. Iterate until green.
acceptance_criteria:
GATED EXIT — all must hold:
1. `cargo test -p auxide-io` green; `cargo clippy -p auxide-io -- -D warnings` clean.
2. `get_best_sample_rate` is now called by play/play_handle (proves wiring) OR removed — `grep -rn "get_best_sample_rate" src/` shows a call site.
3. `channel_router` is referenced by the adapter/StreamController (proves wiring) OR removed.
4. `handle_partial_block` / `handle_unknown_buffer_size` are either implemented (called in the adapter) or deleted; `grep -rn "handle_partial_block\|handle_unknown_buffer_size" src/` shows calls or no definitions.
5. The `Paused` state is made meaningful (distinct from Stopped, e.g., continues emitting the last buffer/silence per a defined contract) OR documented as aliased to Stopped and removed.

title: Fix overstated forbid(alloc) claim (apply or correct docs)
description:
Fix the overstated forbid(alloc) claim. The crate implies RT-alloc-free safety, but the audio callback uses `eprintln!` (allocates) and cpal callbacks may allocate on some paths. Either make the RT path genuinely forbid(alloc) (no logging/alloc in callback) or correct the docs to state the honest guarantee (alloc-light except diagnostics, removed per auxide-io-2d0).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `cargo test -p auxide-io` green; clippy clean.
2. The crate root doc / any forbid(alloc) claim is reconciled: either real `#![forbid(alloc)]` compiles (after removing eprintln per auxide-io-2d0) OR doc corrected to state callback is alloc-light with diagnostics removed, no false "forbid(alloc)" wording.
3. grep for "forbid(alloc)"/"alloc-free" in docs returns only accurate statements.

## Design
A. Coordinate with auxide-io-2d0 (remove eprintln).
B. After that, attempt `#![forbid(alloc)]`; if cpal forces alloc, correct lib.rs doc to "RT callback is allocation-free except where the host API requires it; diagnostics use lock-free atomics."
C. Remove any false claim. Grep-check docs. Iterate.
design:
PLAN:
A. Coordinate with auxide-io-2d0 (remove eprintln from callback).
B. After that, attempt `#![forbid(alloc)]`; if cpal forces alloc, instead correct lib.rs doc to: "RT callback is allocation-free except where the host API requires it; diagnostics use lock-free atomics, not logging."
C. Remove any `#![forbid(alloc)]` that doesn't compile or any doc claiming it falsely.
D. Grep-check docs. Iterate until green.
acceptance_criteria:
GATED EXIT — all must hold:
1. `cargo test -p auxide-io` green; `cargo clippy -p auxide-io -- -D warnings` clean.
2. The crate root doc / any `forbid(alloc)` claim is reconciled: either a real `#![forbid(alloc)]` compiles (after removing eprintln per auxide-io-2d0 and any other alloc in the callback path) OR the doc is corrected to state the callback is alloc-light with diagnostics removed, with no false "forbid(alloc)" wording.
3. grep for "forbid(alloc)" / "alloc-free" in docs returns only accurate statements.

title: Add teardown and restart API (Drop or recreate after error)
description:
Add an explicit teardown/restart API. StreamController owns `stream: Option<Stream>` but offers only `stop` (pause) and no real teardown or recreate-after-error. Add `dispose()` (drop the stream) and a clean `restart()` so callers can recover after errors (ties to auxide-io-m71).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `cargo test -p auxide-io` green; clippy clean.
2. NEW `dispose(&mut self)`: takes stream out and drops it, sets Stopped; after dispose `has_stream()` is false.
3. NEW `restart(&mut self) -> Result<()>`: rebuilds stream (reuse build path) and returns to Running (device-less fixture testable).
4. Unit test `dispose_then_restart` on a stream-less fixture asserts Stopped→Running, no panic.

## Design
A. Refactor stream creation into `build_stream(...)` (shared with m71 recover).
B. `pub fn dispose(&mut self)` -> stream=None; state=Stopped.
C. `pub fn restart(&mut self) -> Result<()>` calls build_stream + start().
D. Add `#[cfg(test)] dispose_then_restart`. Iterate.
design:
PLAN:
A. Refactor stream creation into `build_stream(...)` (shared with auxide-io-m71 recover).
B. Add `pub fn dispose(&mut self)` -> `self.stream = None; self.state.set_state(Stopped);`.
C. Add `pub fn restart(&mut self) -> Result<()>` that calls build_stream and start().
D. Add `#[cfg(test)] dispose_then_restart` against a fixture. Iterate until green.
acceptance_criteria:
GATED EXIT — all must hold:
1. `cargo test -p auxide-io` green; `cargo clippy -p auxide-io -- -D warnings` clean.
2. NEW `dispose(&mut self)`: takes the stream out and drops it, sets state Stopped; after dispose, `has_stream()` is false.
3. NEW `restart(&mut self) -> Result<()>`: rebuilds the stream (reuse the build path) and returns to Running (device-less fixture testable).
4. Unit test `dispose_then_restart` on a stream-less fixture asserts state transitions Stopped→Running and no panic.

title: Report stream latency via OutputCallbackInfo timestamp
description:

B. Add `pub fn latency(&self) -> Option<f64>`.
C. Make run_callback unit-callable (pure fn over buffers) for the test, feeding a constructed OutputCallbackInfo.
D. Add `#[cfg(test)]` latency capture test. Iterate.
design:
PLAN:
A. Refactor the callback (with auxide-io-9k4) so the shared `run_callback` accepts `info: &OutputCallbackInfo` and stores `info.timestamp()`/latency into a field/atomic on StreamController (via a shared Arc or return value).
B. Add `pub fn latency(&self) -> Option<f64>`.
C. Make `run_callback` unit-callable (pure fn over buffers) for the test, feeding a constructed `OutputCallbackInfo`.
D. Add `#[cfg(test)]` latency capture test. Iterate until green.

title: Add latency and glitch benchmarks (replace fuzz claims with a real harness)
description:
Add a real latency/glitch benchmark harness to replace the "fuzz" claims in buffer_size_adapter.rs tests (they are deterministic, not fuzz). Provide a criterion benchmark that measures per-callback cost and counts glitches (ring under/overflow) over many blocks, with an asserted budget.

3. NEW `no_glitches_normal_sizing`: run adapter 1000 host buffers with correct sizing, assert zero underflow/overflow (glitch counter).
4. Benchmark documents budget (e.g., <1 ms/block @64); no false "fuzz" language remains.

## Design
A. Add glitch counter (plain/atomic) returned from fill_host_buffer.
B. Add `[[bench]] name="latency_bench" harness=false` + criterion dev-dep.
C. Add `#[cfg(test)] no_glitches_normal_sizing`. Remove "fuzz" wording. Iterate.
design:
PLAN:

title: Implement real error recovery (rebuild or renegotiate stream on device error)
description:
Implement real error recovery. Today src/error_recovery.rs only silences the buffer and the error callback (stream_controller.rs:293) merely sets an atomic flag. There is no path to rebuild or renegotiate the stream after a device error, so a transient xrun/device-drop leaves audio dead until manual restart.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `cargo test -p auxide-io` green; clippy clean.
2. `StreamController` gains `recover() -> Result<()>` that stops the current stream, re-queries the device via `get_best_sample_rate` + `default_output_device`, and recreates the cpal stream.
3. NEW `recover_clears_error_flag`: simulate error, call `recover()` on a stream-less fixture, assert `has_error()` cleared and state Running.
4. The device error callback sets the flag AND flags recovery (documented contract), not silent death.

## Design
A. Refactor stream creation into private `build_stream(...)` used by play/play_handle and recover.
B. `pub fn recover(&mut self) -> Result<()>`: rebuild via build_stream; reset error_flag; set Running.
C. Error callback sets error_flag + a `recovery_needed` atomic.
D. Add `#[cfg(test)] recover_clears_error_flag`. Iterate.
design:
PLAN:
A. Refactor stream creation into a private `build_stream(&device, sample_rate, block_size, state, error_flag) -> Result<Stream>` used by both `play`/`play_handle` and `recover`.
B. Add `pub fn recover(&mut self) -> Result<()>`: take the runtime/handle out (StreamController currently owns Runtime by value in `play`; for `play_handle` it owns the handle — store it so recover can rebuild). Re-run build_stream; on success reset error_flag and set Running.
C. Make the error callback set error_flag AND (optionally) a `recovery_needed` atomic the main thread can poll.
D. Add the `#[cfg(test)]` `recover_clears_error_flag` against a stream-less fixture (construct StreamController { stream: None, .. }). Iterate until green.
acceptance_criteria:
GATED EXIT — all must hold:
1. `cargo test -p auxide-io` green; `cargo clippy -p auxide-io -- -D warnings` clean.
2. `StreamController` gains a `recover() -> Result<()>` (or `rebuild_stream()`) that stops the current stream, re-queries the device via `get_best_sample_rate` + `default_output_device`, and recreates the cpal stream with the same runtime/handle.
3. NEW test `recover_clears_error_flag`: simulate an error by setting `error_flag`, call `recover()` on a controller whose stream is None (or a test fixture), assert `has_error()` is cleared and `state` returns to Running. (Device-less path must be unit-testable without a real audio device.)
4. The device error callback sets the flag AND schedules/flags a recovery (documented contract), not silent death.

title: Add sample-rate negotiation or resampling via get_best_sample_rate
description:
Wire sample-rate negotiation through `get_best_sample_rate` (already implemented in stream_controller.rs:27 but unused). Today `play`/`play_handle` hard-match `sample_rate == runtime.sample_rate`, which fails or misbehaves when the device can't honor it. Negotiate the best supported rate and either rebuild the runtime at that rate or insert a resampler.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `cargo test -p auxide-io` green; clippy clean.
2. `get_best_sample_rate` has a test proving it returns a supported rate (add if missing).
3. NEW `negotiate_config(device, requested_rate) -> Result<SupportedStreamConfig>` used by play/play_handle; when negotiated != requested, chosen config uses the negotiated rate.
4. If negotiated rate differs from runtime rate, a resampler is applied in BufferSizeAdapter OR runtime rebuilt at negotiated rate; test asserts no panic and play selects negotiated config (device-less unit test).

## Design
A. Extract `negotiate_config(device, requested)` calling get_best_sample_rate then finding the matching SupportedStreamConfig.
B. In play/play_handle replace inline find with negotiate_config; if mismatch, pass negotiated rate and add linear resampler in BufferSizeAdapter.
C. Add `#[cfg(test)] negotiate_config` (mock/skip-if-no-device). Iterate.

title: Make channel routing real (use channel_router, support arbitrary mapping)
description:
Make channel routing real. channel_router.rs provides `duplicate_mono_to_stereo` but StreamController hardcodes `channels: 2` duplication in fill_host_buffer(_handle). Support an arbitrary ChannelMap (mono→[L,R], N outputs, or custom source→destination) so a mono runtime can target any output layout.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `cargo test -p auxide-io` green; clippy clean.
2. NEW `ChannelMap` (channel_router.rs) supporting MonoToStereo and explicit `Vec<(src_ch, dst_ch)>`; fill_host_buffer uses it instead of hardcoded channels=2.
3. NEW `channel_map_routes_correctly`: MonoToStereo → L==R==input; custom map routing source to dst ch 3 only → only that channel carries signal.
4. Default remains MonoToStereo (back-compat).

## Design
A. Add `pub enum ChannelMap { MonoToStereo, Explicit(Vec<(usize,usize)>) }` + `fn apply(&self, sample, dst: &mut [f32])`.
B. Give BufferSizeAdapter an optional ChannelMap (default MonoToStereo); use in fill_host_buffer(_handle).
C. Expose `StreamController::with_channel_map(...)`.
D. Add `#[cfg(test)]` routing tests. Iterate.

title: Add tempo or transport-linked timing hook
description:
Add a tempo/transport-linked timing hook so the callback can be told about transport position (BPM / beat phase) for sample-accurate scheduling. Today the callback has no notion of musical time.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `cargo test -p auxide-io` green; clippy clean.
2. NEW `TransportClock` trait with `transport_time() -> TransportTime { bpm, beat_phase, sample }`, invoked once per host buffer in the shared callback.
3. NEW `transport_advances`: a test impl returns ever-increasing `sample` and beat_phase wrapping at 1.0; assert callback/adapter calls it each block and value advances by host_len.
4. Default no-op impl provided so existing callers unaffected.

## Design
A. Define `pub trait TransportClock { fn transport_time(&self) -> TransportTime; }` (+ struct) in lib/stream_controller.
B. In shared callback (9k4), call clock once per buffer; expose last value via field.
C. `set_transport_clock` on StreamController (default identity clock).
D. Add `#[cfg(test)] transport_advances`. Iterate.
